newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT - Hang Seng seen atop 15,000 by end 97.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Hang Seng seen atop 15,000 by end 97.

text.p: DBS Securities Hong Kong said the Hong Kong stock market's bull run is likely to make a brief pause, but added the outlook is optmistic with the Hang Seng Index targetting the 15,000-15,500 territory by the end of 1997.
"Being grossly overbought, the Hang Seng Index is likely to make a brief pause, moving sideways within the 12,600-13,500 range for the near term," DBS said in a statement on Monday.

But, "the outlook for the new year is outright optimistic, blostered by a highly favourable marco-environment, solid corporate earnings growth, positive impact of the 1997 change-over," said Percy Au-Young, director of research at DBS.
Hong Kong will revert to Chinese sovereignty in mid-1997.
"Our forecasting model calls for the index to rise to 15,000-15,500 by the end of 1997," Au-Young said.
DBS noted Hong Kong's employment rate had improved, private consumption was recovering, the external sector had bottomed out and local residential prices had soared to 1994 record levels.
The brokerage house said it is overweight on the conglomerate, consumer play, hotel, infrastructure and property sectors in the coming quarter.
It said infrastructure remains a bargain and strongly recommended Road King Infrastructure Ltd, Cheung Kong Infrastructure Holdings Ltd, New World Infrastructure Ltd, and Anhui Expressway Co Ltd.
DBS also said it downgraded to neutral the weightings of banks, China-related red chip conglomerates and airline.
Companies in these sectors were in general getting pricey despite their sound foundamentals, and airline stocks were also seen hurt by high fuel price.
But it favoured HSBC Holdings Plc, Guandgong Investment Ltd and China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd.
The brokerage expected these stocks to outperform the market by 10-15 percent.
Utility and telecommunications stocks still seemed uninspiring, it said.
